project_name: King County Library System Administration Module
initial_requirements: King County Library System needs a central administration module for its multi-branch Integrated Library System. System administrators should be able to configure library processes, manage users, groups, and privileges, monitor and troubleshoot servers, databases, applications, services, and interfaces, coordinate software updates, and protect operational data through backup and recovery. The module must support centralized administration without disrupting daily library services.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the most important outcomes this central administration module must achieve for King County Library System, and how will you judge whether it has successfully met those goals?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The biggest outcome is that our system team can manage the whole library network from one place without interrupting branch operations, because service continuity is critical. It also needs to make administration faster and more reliable for user access, configuration changes, monitoring, updates, and backup or recovery, so staff spend less time reacting to problems and more time preventing them.
We’d judge success by whether administrators can do those tasks consistently across all branches, whether incidents and downtime are reduced, and whether routine changes can be completed without affecting patrons or circulation work. If it gives us better visibility into problems and a safer way to recover data and services when something fails, that would be a strong sign it’s meeting the goal.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Who are the specific stakeholder roles that will use or depend on this central administration module, and what responsibilities or permissions should each role have?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main users will be system administrators, and they’d need broad access to configure processes, manage users, groups, and privileges, monitor the environment, and handle backups and recovery. We’d also expect IT operations or support staff to use it for troubleshooting and coordinating updates, but probably with narrower permissions than a full administrator.
Library branch managers and other business staff would likely depend on it indirectly rather than using it every day, so they may only need limited visibility into service status or incidents if that’s part of their role. I don’t know yet exactly how we’d split permissions between those groups, so we’d want to define that more carefully with the library’s IT and security teams.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What audit logging and change traceability requirements do you need for this module—for example, which administrative actions must be logged, what details should each record capture, how long logs should be retained, and who should be able to review or report on them?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
We need a full audit trail for anything that changes access, configuration, or operational state, so things like user and group changes, privilege updates, process configuration, server or service changes, updates, backup and recovery actions, and failed login or access attempts. Each record should capture who did it, when it happened, what system or branch it affected, what was changed before and after, and whether it succeeded or failed.
Retention and review rules aren’t fully decided yet, but we’d want logs kept long enough to support troubleshooting, security review, and any internal or legal retention needs. Usually only authorized administrators and security or audit personnel should be able to review detailed logs or generate reports, with access tightly controlled.

turns.interviewer_utterance: For the monitoring and alerting functions, what specific systems, services, and metrics should the module track, and how should alerts be delivered and escalated (for example, by email, SMS, dashboard, or ticketing) for different types or severities of issues?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
We’d want it to track the core pieces that keep the library system running: servers, databases, application services, interfaces between systems, and the status of scheduled jobs or backups. Key metrics would be availability, error rates, performance or response time, resource usage like CPU and disk, and any service failures or communication breakdowns between systems.
For alerts, the module should definitely show issues on a dashboard, and for higher-severity problems it should notify the right support people directly, probably by email and maybe SMS for urgent outages. Escalation would depend on severity and time of day, but I don’t know the exact rules yet, so that would need to be defined with operations and support staff.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When the module detects a service or system problem, how should it represent the catalog of services and their dependencies, and what end-to-end incident workflow or case management process should administrators and support staff follow from detection through resolution and closure?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
It should present a clear service view that shows each major service, what it depends on, and what downstream systems might be affected, so an administrator can quickly see the likely impact of a failure. I’d expect that to be more of a practical dependency map or service tree than a technical diagram, with enough detail to trace problems without overwhelming staff.
For the incident workflow, it should go from detection to acknowledgment, assignment, investigation, containment, fix, verification, and then closure with notes on what happened and what was done. Support staff should be able to create or update a case, add comments, attach evidence, and mark the incident resolved, while administrators can escalate or coordinate across teams if the issue spans servers, applications, or interfaces.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Enable the system team to centrally manage the whole library network from one place without interrupting branch operations; make administration faster and more reliable for user access, configuration changes, monitoring, updates, and backup/recovery; reduce incidents and downtime; and improve visibility into problems plus safer recovery of data and services when failures occur.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Primary users are system administrators with broad access to configure processes, manage users/groups/privileges, monitor the environment, and handle backups and recovery. IT operations/support staff also use the module for troubleshooting and coordinating updates with narrower permissions. Library branch managers and other business staff depend on it indirectly and may only need limited visibility into service status or incidents.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Centralized administration across all branches; configure library processes; manage users, groups, and privileges; monitor the environment; troubleshoot servers, databases, applications, services, and interfaces; coordinate software updates; perform backup and recovery; provide service status or incident visibility for limited users; track servers, databases, application services, interfaces, scheduled jobs, and backups; display issues on a dashboard and notify support staff for high-severity problems; present a clear service view with dependencies; support incident workflow from detection through acknowledgment, assignment, investigation, containment, fix, verification, and closure; allow comments, evidence attachments, resolution notes, and escalation across teams.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: System administrators require broad privileges for configuration, access management, monitoring, backup, and recovery, while IT operations/support should have narrower permissions. Branch managers and business staff should have limited visibility only if needed. Permission splits and access rules need to be defined with IT and security teams.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Users, groups, privileges, configuration/process settings, server records, database records, application records, service records, interface records, incidents/problems, update/maintenance information, backup/recovery data, scheduled jobs, metrics such as availability, error rates, response time, resource usage, and service failure/communication breakdown data.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Centralized administration must not disrupt daily library services or patron/circulation work. Permissions must be appropriately restricted by role. Exact permission boundaries are still to be defined with IT and security teams.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Must support service continuity and avoid disrupting patron or circulation work; improve reliability, visibility into problems, and safe recovery capabilities; reduce incidents and downtime; allow routine changes without affecting branch operations; and provide dashboard visibility and timely alerts for issues.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: Routine changes and administrative actions should not affect patrons or circulation work. Branch managers and business staff are not expected to use the system daily and may only receive limited visibility into status or incidents.

slots.name: availability_and_maintenance_windows
slots.value: Not specified; updates and administrative changes should be coordinated so they do not interrupt branch operations.

slots.name: backup_retention_and_recovery_objectives
slots.value: Backups and recovery must protect operational data and provide a safer way to recover data and services when failures occur. Specific retention periods and recovery targets are not yet defined.

slots.name: audit_logging_and_change_traceability
slots.value: A full audit trail is required for changes to access, configuration, or operational state, including user and group changes, privilege updates, process configuration, server or service changes, updates, backup and recovery actions, and failed login or access attempts. Each log should capture who performed the action, when it occurred, what system or branch was affected, before-and-after values, and whether it succeeded or failed. Logs should be retained long enough for troubleshooting, security review, and any legal or internal retention needs, and detailed logs or reports should be restricted to authorized administrators and security or audit personnel.

slots.name: alerting_and_escalation_rules
slots.value: The module should provide dashboard visibility for issues and notify the right support people directly for higher-severity problems, probably by email and possibly SMS for urgent outages. Escalation should depend on severity and time of day, but the exact rules are not yet defined.

slots.name: integration_dependencies_and_interfaces
slots.value: Must support monitoring and troubleshooting of servers, databases, applications, services, interfaces, scheduled jobs, and backups. Specific external systems or integration details are not yet defined.

slots.name: monitoring_scope_and_metrics
slots.value: Track servers, databases, application services, interfaces between systems, scheduled jobs, and backups. Key metrics include availability, error rates, response time, resource usage such as CPU and disk, service failures, and communication breakdowns between systems.

slots.name: service_catalog_and_dependency_model
slots.value: Provide a clear service view showing each major service, what it depends on, and what downstream systems might be affected. The preferred representation is a practical dependency map or service tree rather than a highly technical diagram, with enough detail to trace problems without overwhelming staff.

slots.name: incident_workflow_and_case_management
slots.value: Incident handling should follow detection, acknowledgment, assignment, investigation, containment, fix, verification, and closure with notes on what happened and what was done. Support staff should be able to create or update a case, add comments, attach evidence, and mark incidents resolved, while administrators can escalate or coordinate across teams when issues span servers, applications, or interfaces.

slots.name: role_based_access_control_matrix
slots.value: Not yet defined. System administrators need broad access; IT operations/support need narrower permissions; branch managers and business staff should have limited visibility only if needed. Exact role-to-permission boundaries still need to be defined with IT and security teams.

slots.name: maintenance_change_approval_process
slots.value: Not specified. Administrative changes and updates should be coordinated so they do not interrupt branch operations.

slots.name: backup_encryption_and_access_controls
slots.value: Not specified beyond requiring restricted access. Backup and recovery actions should be protected as part of the full audit trail and only accessible to authorized administrators and security or audit personnel where appropriate.

slots.name: disaster_recovery_site_and_failover_strategy
slots.value: Not specified. The requirement only states that data and services must be recoverable safely when failures occur.

slots.name: operational_reporting_and_executive_dashboards
slots.value: Not specified beyond operational visibility. The module should display issues on a dashboard and support visibility into service status or incidents for limited users.

slots.name: user_account_lifecycle_and_provisioning
slots.value: Not specified. The module must support managing users, groups, and privileges, but detailed account lifecycle processes are not yet defined.

slots.name: notification_channels_and_delivery_preferences
slots.value: Alerts should appear on a dashboard and, for high-severity issues, be delivered directly to support staff by email and possibly SMS for urgent outages.
